bottleneck: Partial reprogramming with Yamanaka factors rejuvenates aged cells, but the line between rejuvenation and dedifferentiation is thin: overshoot produces pluripotent cells that form teratomas, while undershoot does nothing measurable. Controlling dose, duration, and tissue specificity in vivo is unsolved, and the epigenetic clock mechanisms being reset are incompletely understood, so there is no biomarker confirming safe, on-target rejuvenation. Delivering the factors to aged tissues without systemic exposure adds another unsolved layer.
current_state: Cyclic partial reprogramming extends healthspan in progeroid mice. Human translation is preclinical, gated by the teratoma risk and delivery control problems that no protocol has resolved.

sources.title: Gene Therapy: A Breakthrough in Disease Treatment

title: Partial reprogramming risks teratomas in vivo
why_it_blocks: Cellular rejuvenation is the closest thing to an aging cure in mammals, but a rejuvenation therapy that can cause tumors is unusable. Control — not the factors themselves — is the missing piece, and control is everything.
